title: Godot CLI export fails with an opaque error message when folder on provided `--path` does not exist
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: `4.2.1.stable.official.b09f793f5`

### System information

Godot v4.2.1.stable - macOS 26.2.0 - GLES3 (Compatibility) - Apple M1 Max - Apple M1 Max (10 Threads)

### Issue description

When attempting to export a project via the command line, I provided an output path value to that was erroneously missing a folder. When I did so, the output I saw had two problems:

1. It did not notify me that a folder on the path was missing
2. It said that the export both failed and completed.

```
$ godot --headless --verbose --path godot --export-release Web priv/static/godot/bridge.html
Exporting Godot project for web...
WARNING: Custom cursor shape not supported by this display server.
     at: cursor_set_custom_image (servers/display_server.cpp:505)
WARNING: Blend file import is enabled in the project settings, but no Blender path is configured in the editor settings. Blend files will not be imported.
     at: _editor_init (modules/gltf/register_types.cpp:63)
ERROR: Project export for preset "Web" failed.
   at: _fs_changed (editor/editor_node.cpp:994)
Godot export complete → priv/static/godot/bridge.html
```

In the above example, `priv/static` existed, but `priv/static/godot` did not. Note that two different messages are shown:

1. The export failed message: `ERROR: Project export for preset "Web" failed.`
2. and the export completed message: `Godot export complete → priv/static/godot/bridge.html`

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a new project (e.g. in directory `project1`)
2. Ensure export templates are downloaded
3. Create an export template called `Web`
4. Attempt to export the project to a nonexistent directory (e.g. `export/project1.html`) with a command like this:

```shell
godot --headless --verbose --path ./project1 --export-release Web ./export/project1.html
```

N/A
